payload.native_system_prompt:
You are part of an optimization system that improves a given text (i.e. the variable). You are the gradient (feedback) engine. Your only responsibility is to give intelligent and creative feedback and constructive criticism to variables, given an objective specified in <OBJECTIVE_FUNCTION> </OBJECTIVE_FUNCTION> tags. The variables may be solutions to problems, prompts to language models, code, or any other text-based variable. Pay attention to the role description of the variable, and the context in which it is used. You should assume that the variable will be used in a similar context in the future. Only provide strategies, explanations, and methods to change in the variable. DO NOT propose a new version of the variable, that will be the job of the optimizer. Your only job is to send feedback and criticism (compute 'gradients'). For instance, feedback can be in the form of 'Since language models have the X failure mode...', 'Adding X can fix this error because...', 'Removing X can improve the objective function because...', 'Changing X to Y would fix the mistake ...', that gets at the downstream objective.
If a variable is already working well (e.g. the objective function is perfect, an evaluation shows the response is accurate), you should not give feedback.

### Glossary of tags that will be sent to you:
# - <LM_SYSTEM_PROMPT>: The system prompt for the language model.
# - <LM_INPUT>: The input to the language model.
# - <LM_OUTPUT>: The output of the language model.
# - <OBJECTIVE_FUNCTION>: The objective of the optimization task.
# - <VARIABLE>: Specifies the span of the variable.
# - <ROLE>: The role description of the variable.
payload.instruction: transform the black DVD into a white DVD
payload.rubric: Judge requested image editing: yes means all requested changes are complete, no means no requested change has progressed, partial means some progress without complete fulfillment. Unrelated edits are not requested progress. Insufficient evidence stays unresolved.

node.question: Change the black DVD to white while retaining its identity as a DVD.
node.criteria: Judge only the requested transformation, using both support observations. Return yes when the DVD is visibly white rather than black and retains its identity as a DVD. Return no only when there is sufficient evidence that no requested change has progressed—for example, the DVD remains black and retains its identity. Return partial when the color change has progressed but the DVD is not yet white, or when the DVD is white but its identity as a DVD has been lost. Unrelated edits do not count. If the evidence does not establish one of these outcomes, return unresolved. Support observations are evidence, not independent completion credit.
node.binding: Target: The DVD is visibly white rather than black.. Reference: The black DVD in the input image..

response.content: {"text":"The node’s binding is too vague and its completion criterion is being satisfied by generic disc-like appearance rather than verifying the *same DVD* from the source. In the edited image, the source DVD’s small rectangular case/printed object is no longer apparent; two white circular objects are visible, including one near the black object, so the traces’ confident claim that the DVD is white and retains its identity is not adequately grounded. Tighten the binding to track the source DVD across images and require evidence that the edited white object corresponds to that source target and remains identifiable specifically as a DVD, not merely as a disc. Evaluate color change and identity separately, then combine them using the stated complete/partial/no/unresolved distinctions; do not treat passing support observations as automatic completion credit. The repeated high-confidence yes traces suggest a systematic target-binding or criterion failure, not a transport/schema issue. Do not force the reference label: inspect the visual evidence and preserve unresolved when correspondence or identity cannot be established."}
